title: registerUser: sign-up outcomes
scope: Graph one call of the registerUser server action with Supabase and the request headers replaced by test doubles. Field validation and the confirmation link are one decision each; "hidden duplicate" (no error, user returned with no identities) is one compound decision because Supabase reports it as one case.
complexity: Cyclomatic complexity V(G) = 20 - 15 + 2 = 7. Six decisions (G1, G3, G6, G7, G9, G11) also give 6 + 1 = 7.

Evidence: tests/lab4/auth-profile-basis-path.test.ts (describe "registerUser") and evidence/auth-profile-basis-path-observations.json. Supabase is a test double; no account was created.

title: deleteAccount: obligation checks, soft delete and undo
scope: Graph one call of deleteAccount with valid ports. Each canDeactivate call is one predicate; its six obligation conditions are tested separately by the black-box table. An exception anywhere in the try block follows the same catch edges as the login-removal failure at A6.
complexity: Cyclomatic complexity V(G) = 15 - 12 + 2 = 5. Four decisions (A1, A4, A6, A8) also give 4 + 1 = 5.
paths: 1 active commitment at the first check. BLOCKED; only the check runs; profile stays ACTIVE.
A0 A1 A3 A4 A6 A7 A11
Nothing outstanding at either check. DELETED; check, deactivate, check, delete-login; profile INACTIVE.
A0 A1 A3 A4 A5 A11
Clear first; 100c available at the re-check. Profile restored ACTIVE; BLOCKED.
A0 A1 A3 A4 A6 A8 A9 A11
Login removal throws; restore succeeds. Original error rethrown; profile ACTIVE.
A0 A1 A3 A4 A6 A8 A10 A11
Login removal and restore both throw. AggregateError with 2 errors; profile left INACTIVE.
notes: Each path adds at least one edge the earlier paths did not use, and together the five paths use all 15 edges.
D3 is the race the re-check exists for: money or a commitment arriving between the page check and deletion.

Evidence: tests/lab4/account-basis-path.test.ts (describe "deleteAccount") and evidence/account-basis-path-observations.json. Path strings are predictions from the source; the expected and actual outcomes, steps and profile states were executed. No branch instrumentation was run.

title: Joining a group through its invitation link
scope: Graph one call of ManageGroup.join, including RegularGroup.join, with a valid user ID. "Link active and token matches" is one compound predicate: the group is looked up by its token, so the mismatched-token operand cannot be reached through this entry point.
complexity: Cyclomatic complexity V(G) = 14 - 11 + 2 = 5. Four decisions (J1, J3, J5, J7) also give 4 + 1 = 5.
paths: Token that matches no group. INVALID_INVITATION; nothing saved; members unchanged.
Old link of an archived group. INVALID_STATE; nothing saved.
J0 J1 J3 J5 J6 J10
Active group whose link was turned off. INVALID_INVITATION; nothing saved.
J0 J1 J3 J5 J7 J8 J10
The owner opens the valid link. ALREADY_MEMBER; nothing saved.
J0 J1 J3 J5 J7 J9 J10
A new user opens the valid link. JOINED; saved once; members owner and newcomer.
notes: Each path adds at least one edge the earlier paths did not use, and together the five paths use all 14 edges.
J4 confirms that joining twice is harmless: no second membership and no save.
Evidence: tests/lab4/account-basis-path.test.ts (describe "ManageGroup") and evidence/account-basis-path-observations.json. The group store is the in-memory test double; no database was used.
